To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the jet quenching in heavy ion collisions can be described by a simple model with a few free parameters and the jet quench ing effect is stronger for smaller jet transverse momentum.
the suppression of inclusive jet production and the flattening of dijet imbalance are the most important signatures of jet-medium interactions in high-energy nuclear collision s.
the suppression of inclusive jet and the broadening of dijet momentum imbalance are observed in the presence of the hot and dense QCP matter.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the production of jets and their properties in high-energy heavy-ion collisions.
the study of jet properties in heavy ion collisions and the jet-medium interactions.
the study of the properties of the hot and dense medium produced in high-energy nuclear reactions by measuring jets.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the jet energy loss in QGP can be extracted from the jet spectra and jet shapes, while the jet modification by initial-state effects can be extracted from dijet momentum imbalance.
the jet-medium interactions in heavy ion collisions can be well described by the jet energy loss mechanism.
the jet quenching effect is a strong evidence for the creation of a hot and de nse QCD medium in high-energy nuclear collision.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the jet quenching effects in the hot and dense QED matter are significant and should be considered in the study of high-energy collisions.
jets can be a good probe of hot QCD matter and jet quenching is a powerful tool to extract the medium transport coefficient in high-energy nuclear reactions.
jet quenching in the hot and dense medium can be well understood by the parton energy loss formalism.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the parton energy loss effect is the most dominant factor to modify the jet production cross section in heavy-ion collisions, which is also the key to the study of jet quenching.
the jet-medium interaction is the dominant effect for the modification of jets in heavy-ion collisions, and the energy loss of jets is the main source of the jet modification.
, by measuring jet spectra, one can probe the medium-induced jet energy loss and the medium properties such as the transport coefficient.
